Chapter 5 (al-bāb al-khāmis): On the secrets of In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate and the hidden secrets and blessings that belong to it [51]

Know — may God grant you success in obedience to Him — that whoever knows what God, glorified and exalted, has deposited of secrets within "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", and writes them, will not be burned by fire; and likewise whoever writes it and arranges it as a wafq will not be burned by fire. It has been related that when "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" was sent down, the mountains shook at its descent, and the Zabāniya (the angels who guard the Fire) said: Whoever recites it will not enter the Fire. And it is nineteen letters, according to the number of the angels charged with the Fire — may God, exalted is He, grant us refuge from it. And whoever makes frequent mention of it is granted awe-inspiring dignity (hayba) before the celestial world and the terrestrial. And it is the first thing that the celestial Pen traced upon the surface of the

Tablet, and it is that by which God established the kingdom of Solomon son of David — peace be upon him. So whoever writes it 600 times and carries it with him is granted awe-inspiring dignity in the hearts of created beings. And it is related of ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them both — that he said: Whoever has a need of God, exalted is He, let him fast on Wednesday /fol. 27r./ and Thursday and Friday; and when Friday comes, let him purify himself and go early to the congregational mosque and give alms, be they small or great, from a loaf of bread down to less than that — and whoever gives more, that is better. Then, when he has prayed the Friday prayer, after it let him say: "O God, I ask You by Your name 'In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate', who — there is no god but He, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed; He is the All-Merciful, the Compassionate (Q 59:22). And I ask You by Your name 'In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate', He of whom there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting; neither slumber seizes Him nor sleep; to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth (Q 2:255). And I ask You by Your name 'In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate', before which faces are bowed low, before which voices are hushed, and hearts tremble in awe of Him. And I ask You to bless and give peace to our master Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, and to fulfil my need, which is such-and-such" — and he names it. And he used to say: Do not teach it to the foolish, lest they invoke it one against another and be answered.

And it is related from the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — that he said: ((Between "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" and the Greatest Name of God there is only what lies between the black of the eye and the white of it.)) And the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((The veil between the children of Adam and the satans is "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate".)) So bi-sm ("in the name of") is the concealed name that indicates that after it comes the Greatest Name, which is Allāh. For this name is the Name of Majesty (ism al-jalāla); it is the name of the exalted Essence; it is the name that gathers the meanings of all the Most Beautiful Names; it is the sovereign of all the names, and to it they return. It stands to the names as the proper name (ʿalam) does, for if you are asked, "Who is al-Raḥmān?" you say: "God." And likewise all the rest of the names are annexed to it and are known by the Name of Majesty, by the loftiness of its elevation and by its glory. And it has a nobility over and above the [other] names, namely this: that if you remove from it the letter alif, there remains li-llāh ("to God"); if you remove from it the first lām, there remains lahu ("to Him"); and if you remove from it the second lām, there remains hū ("He"). So every letter of it is a name subsisting in itself, which is not the case with any other of the names; for if you remove a letter from one of those, its meaning is nullified, whereas this Greatest Name stands firm with its letters and its meaning is not disturbed. So it has a nobility above all the rest of the names, and a proof that it is the name of the honoured Essence, established in might and in permanence. And it has yet another nobility: it points to the Essence that is single and odd-numbered, and it points to the declaration of the oneness of the Godhead. For its first [letter] is the alif, which is the first of the letters and the first of the numbers of the units; so it is single in its quality and one in its number, pointing to the oneness of its Master who created it. And its last is the letter hāʾ, which points to the declaration of the oneness of the Godhead of its Lord; and this is not to be found in any other of the names. And it says, by the tongue of its very state: I am the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward (Q 57:3). Then He, exalted is He, followed it with the attribute of raḥmāniyya and of rāḥimiyya, of mercy and of raḥīmiyya, and so He said, exalted is He: the All-Merciful, the Compassionate (Q 1:1). And for that reason He said, exalted is He: Say: Call upon God, or call upon the All-Merciful; whichever you call upon, to Him belong the Most Beautiful Names (Q 17:110). So He gave you the choice to call upon Him and to say "O God" (Yā Allāh), for it gathers /fol. 27v./ the two attributes of mercy, and each is a noble name. And if you wish to seek mercy, you say "O All-Merciful" (Yā Raḥmān); and it is the most specific of the specific, because Allāh, exalted is He, is by common agreement the most specific of the names and the greatest of them. And it is a Syriac name; as for its interpretation, it is "the Bringer-forth of things from non-existence into existence". And it has meanings which he who looks into them is bound to conceal from the foolish, lest they make of it a means to the doing of reprehensible and forbidden deeds, and so fall from the sight of God, exalted is He — as Balʿām b. Bāʿūrā fell when he intended by it disobedience to God, exalted is He. We take refuge in God from His wrath; and make us not, [O God], of those who seek help by His mighty Name unto disobedience to Him.

And know that this mighty Name has four letters — an alif, two lāms, and a hāʾ — even as the natures are four, and the quarters are four: east, west, qibla, and south; and the angels of glorification are four: Jibrāʾīl, Mīkāʾīl, Isrāfīl, and ʿAzrāʾīl. Jibrāʾīl — peace be upon him — is the bearer of the message to the messengers, and the master of overwhelming victory and subjugation; by him God, exalted is He, destroyed the unbelievers of the nations of old, by the swallowing-up of the earth, by the earthquake, by the thunderbolt, and by the pelting [of stones]. And Isrāfīl — peace be upon him — is the master of the Trumpet and of the blast. He has three blasts: the blast of terror, according to His words, exalted is He, and those in the heavens and those on earth will be terrified, save whom God wills (Q 27:87); and the blast of the thunder-stroke, according to His words, exalted is He, and those in the heavens and those on earth will be struck down (Q 39:68); and the blast of the resurrection, according to His words, exalted is He, then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on (Q 39:68). To each blast belongs a secret proper to it. And ʿAzrāʾīl — peace be upon him — is charged with the seizing of the spirits and their passing away; in him is the crushing of the tyrants, the cutting off of the last remnant of the arrogant and of the wicked oppressors, and in him is the repose of the believer, his arrival at his

Lord, the attainment of his hope, and his joy at what God has prepared for him of His generosity, His bounty, His pardon, His forgiveness, and His mercy. And Mīkāʾīl — peace be upon him — is the one charged with the provisions of the servants, with conveying their dispatch to them, with restoring their last breath of life, and with preserving their existence; so that there is not a grain of sesame in the earth but one of his helpers is charged with it, until he conveys it to its owner. And each one of them has helpers whose number cannot be reckoned; and they have litanies of remembrance (adhkār) and operations suited to them, by which their assistance is obtained. And these four angels have days proper to them. To Jibrāʾīl — peace be upon him — belongs, of the days, Monday, because it is cold and moist. To Isrāfīl — peace be upon him — belongs, of the days, Thursday, and it is hot and moist. To ʿAzrāʾīl — peace be upon him — belongs, of the days, Saturday, since it is of his relation, cold and dry, its nature being earth and death and annihilation. And to Mīkāʾīl — peace be upon him — belongs Wednesday, for it is compounded, having in it something of the four natures. And they have four seals proper to them, the mention of which will follow, if God, exalted is He, wills: the ninefold (al-mutassaʿ) for Jibrāʾīl — peace be upon him — the fourfold (al-murabbaʿ) for Isrāfīl — peace be upon him — the threefold (al-muthallath) for ʿAzrāʾīl — peace be upon him — /fol. 28r./ and the eightfold (al-muthamman) for Mīkāʾīl. As for their awfāq, to which we have alluded, they are as you see.

So when you desire one of the four operations, you write the seal according to its number, its reckoning, and its correctness; and if you add to it the name of the object sought, it is more effective and swifter for what you seek. As for the ninefold, it is written upon white paper (kāghid), or upon pure white silver, on Monday at sunrise, that being the hour of the Moon. If your operation is for good, then write it when the Moon is increasing in light and in reckoning, in its exaltation or in its felicity, safe from the malefics; and you speak over it with what we shall mention to you, for by it you will attain your hope and reach your desire, if there is in it what pleases God. But if it be for an act of disobedience, then part of the deprivation is that no answer comes. And if you desire something other than that — vengeance upon harmful enemies, or upon an oppressor or a tyrant — then let the Moon be in the dark of the month (muḥāq) and in combustion, conjoined with Saturn or with Mars. And beware of teaching it to one who does not deserve it; and beware of vindictive gloating — and refuge is with God, exalted is He. And whoever is patient and forgives — truly that is among the matters demanding firm resolve (Q 42:43). And to him who pardons and sets things right, his reward rests with God (Q 42:40); and whoever defends himself after he has been wronged — against such there is no any way [of blame] against them (Q 42:41). And suffumigate: for a good [end] with sweet-scented fumigants, and for an evil one with their opposite — so understand. If the Moon, at the time of your operation, is in an airy sign, suspend your operation in the wind; and if it is fiery, then in the fire, or you suspend it over the fire. And if the Moon is in a watery sign, suspend it over the water, or bury it beside the water. And if you wish to send it forth, let it be in a case of Persian reed sealed over with wax, and you speak over it the words that come hereafter. And if the Moon is in an earthy sign, then bury your operation in the earth beneath the threshold of his door, or of your own door if you wish to draw him to you; and even were he the caliph, he would answer you and come at your call. So understand.
/fol. 29r./

As for that which you speak over it for good, it is these words. You say: O God, I ask You by all Your Most Beautiful Names, the praiseworthy, the glorious, which, when they are laid upon a thing, it is humbled before them; and when good things are sought by them, they are attained; and when evils are averted by them, they are averted. And [I ask You] by Your perfect words, of which: If all the trees on the earth were pens, and the sea, with seven seas after it to swell it, [were ink], the words of God would not be exhausted. Truly God is Mighty, Wise (Q 31:27). O al-Kāfī (the Sufficient), O al-Walī (the Protecting Friend), O al-ʿAfū (the Pardoner), O al-Raʾūf (the Ever-Kind), O al-Laṭīf (the Subtle), O al-Razzāq (the Provider), O al-Wadūd (the Loving), O al-Fattāḥ (the Opener), O al-Wāsiʿ (the All-Encompassing), O al-Karīm (the Generous), O al-Wahhāb (the Bestower), O al-Bāsiṭ (the Expander), O Dhū al-Ṭawl (Possessor of Bounty), O Dhū al-Faḍl (Possessor of Grace), O al-Muʿṭī (the Giver), O al-Mughnī (the Enricher), O al-Raḥmān (the All-Merciful), O al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate), O al-Ghanī (the Self-Sufficient), O al-Mughīth (the Succourer), O al-Ḥannān (the Tender), O al-Mannān (the Bounteous), O al-Jawād (the Munificent), O al-Munʿim (the Bestower of favours), O al-Muḥsin (the Beneficent). O God, enrich me by what You have made lawful, so that I need not what You have forbidden; and by obedience to You, so that I need not disobedience to You; and by Your bounty, so that I need none besides You. O al-Raḥmān, O al-Raḥīm, O Most Merciful of the merciful. And I ask You, O God, by Your name Allāh, beside whom there is no god but He: al-Jamīl (the Beautiful), al-Raḥmān, al-Raḥīm, al-Laṭīf, al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), al-Raʾūf, al-ʿAfū, al-Ghafūr (the Forgiving), al-Muʾmin (the Granter of Security), al-Muhaymin (the Overseer), al-Mujīb (the Answerer), al-Mughīth, al-Qarīb (the Near), al-Sarīʿ (the Swift), al-Karīm, Dhū al-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Munificence), Dhū al-Ṭawl, al-Mannān.

Know that whoever carries these names, his character is ennobled and he is liberal with generosity and mercy toward people, and people likewise toward him. They behold, of the meanings of subtle kindness (luṭf), wonders on his behalf. There accrues to him acceptance of countenance, and his outward and his inward are made beautiful. In it is the Greatest Name of God, by which, when He is called, He answers, and when He is asked by it, He gives. It is among the mightiest of the litanies of remembrance (adhkār) and the noblest of them, and no one has persevered in its remembrance but that abundant sciences were unveiled to him, and God made easy for him the thing sought and provided him the thing desired in urgent affairs. And whoever remembers them at midnight beholds of the wonders according to the measure of his aspiration (himma). Persevering in them opens the hidden secrets; and no one persists in their remembrance but that he sees, of the affairs of the upper world, a breeze of secrets from the cosmos, and there is made subject to him every world of the angels, of humankind, of the jinn, and of the people of form-fashioning (ahl al-taṣwīr). These are the perfect words, and in them are the marvels of the secrets.

Now His name al-Kāfī: no one invokes it while wishing for a thing his wish has not attained but that God brings him to it from a quarter upon which he does not rely and which does not occur to his mind. Nor does one who is in a feeble rank, while his aspiration seeks something higher than it, invoke it but that God — exalted is He — makes easy for him the attaining of it, not with much toil, nor with the loss of anything of a state he used to find. And whoever perseveres in its remembrance, there returns to him what had been lost to him. As for His name al-Walī: God is the Protecting Friend of the believers. As for His name al-ʿAfū: it is efficacious for repelling what gives pain, whether the pain of religion or that of this world. As for His name al-Raʾūf: it is a remembrance suited to the fearful; none has kept constantly to it but that he has found the coolness of tranquillity and his terror has been stilled. And one who possesses insight has mentioned that whoever perseveres in this remembrance until a state from it comes to prevail over him, upon a stomach empty of food, and then takes hold of fire, it will not harm him; and if he breathes at that moment upon a cooking-pot boiling /fol. 29v./ upon the fire, its boiling subsides by the leave of God, exalted is He — save that he adds to it al-Ḥalīm (the Forbearing), al-Raʾūf, and al-Mannān, saying: "O al-Ḥalīm, O al-Raʾūf, O al-Mannān." And whoever writes this remembrance in the hour of the Moon on Monday, at the beginning of the month, and confronts with it one whose evil he fears, God extinguishes his evil at the sight of him. And no one whom a lust has overpowered perseveres in this remembrance with the three names but that God — exalted is He — plucks the craving out of him in the course of the remembrance.

As for His name al-Laṭīf: how swift it is to dispel anguish in times of hardship! No other name is joined to it. There appears of its effects the most wondrous marvel. No one who is pained by something in his soul or in his body invokes it but that God removes it from him in the course of the remembrance. And no one in whose soul there is a mighty matter that has appalled him — and the like of it in his imagining — and who then sets himself to the remembrance by it while observing that condition, but that he beholds the marvel of it: how it dissolves and melts away, so that he does not rise from his place with anything remaining upon him that he dreads. And that is profitable against all hurts and harms, for their removal and for treatment by it —

namely, that it be written and drunk, for all pains. He writes it 160 times, the number of the numbers of the name that falls upon it. And you spread the name out into letters and write for each letter its number, thus: the alif 142 times, the lām 100 times and two, the ṭāʾ 10 times, the yāʾ 11 times, and the fāʾ 81 times. It repels, it ennobles, and it wards off. As for His names al-Razzāq and al-Wadūd: they are for one who has tasted something of love and has been marked with something of its traces; by them his states are made to grow. So whoever takes the name of the one whose affection he desires, and adds to it al-Wadūd 51 times together with the name of the one sought, and breaks it until that name becomes another name — then you take what lies above it in broken form, and put it on a sheet of paper (qirṭās), and carry it with you, and meet the one whose affection you desire, and he will love you and be led docile to you and follow you: this after you have recited over it this remembrance the stated number of times after writing it, and have suffumigated it with the most fragrant incense, and after you have prayed two rakʿas — the first with the Mother of the Qurʾān (the Fātiḥa) and Sūrat al-Burūj (Q 85), and the second with the Mother of the Qurʾān and the sura Have We not expanded for you (Q 94:1) — 3 times. Then you write it and set it out according to the description we have mentioned, and you will see a wonder from it. And so likewise all the foregoing names.

And it is said: when "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" was sent down, the dwellers of the heavens among the angels rejoiced, and the Throne quivered at its descent, and there descended with it such-and-such a thousand angels, and the angels increased in faith, and the jinn fell prostrate upon their faces, and the celestial spheres were set in motion, and the kingdoms were humbled before its immensity. "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" was written upon the forehead of Adam — peace be upon him — 500 years before he was created; and it was written upon the wing of Gabriel — peace be upon him — on the day he descended upon Abraham the Friend [of God] — peace be upon him — and said: "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate: We said: O fire, be coolness and peace upon Abraham (Q 21:69)." And "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" was written upon the staff of Moses — peace be upon him — and its writing was in Syriac; and but for it the sea would not have been cleft for him. And "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" was written upon the tongue of Jesus son of Mary — peace be upon him — on the day he spoke in the cradle; and he used to utter it over the dead, and they would come to life by the leave of God, exalted is He. And "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" was written upon the signet-ring of Solomon son of David — peace be upon him.

And among its excellences is that it stands at the head of every sura of the Mighty Qurʾān. And when "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" is recited — when a person recites it according to the number of its letters, 584 times, over a period of 7 days, with the intention of some matter — that matter is accomplished, whether it be the drawing of a benefit or the repelling of a harm; or if it be merchandise, it finds a ready sale, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And when "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" is recited at the time of sleep 21 times, he is safe that night from Satan the accursed, and safe from theft and from sudden death; and it repels every affliction. And among the occult properties of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" is that when it is recited in the face of a tyrant 50 times, he is humbled before him, and God — exalted is He — casts awe of him into the heart of that tyrant and despot, and he is safe from his evil. And among the occult properties of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" is that when it is recited 100 times over any pain whatsoever over a period of 3 days, God — exalted is He — removes that pain, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted is He. "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate": and when it is recited at the rising of the sun, while you are facing it, over a period of 3 days, 300 times, and you invoke blessing upon the Prophet, our master Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — 100 times, God — exalted is He — will provide for you from where you do not reckon, and the year will not come round but that God — exalted is He — has enriched you from His bounty; and constancy in what we have mentioned is required. And among the occult properties of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" /fol. 30r./ is that if a prisoner recites it, God — blessed and exalted — grants him relief, even were he held for a slain man, if he recites it every day and night 1,000 times. And when "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" is recited on Friday, while the preacher is upon the pulpit, 113 times, and then he raises his hands and pleads earnestly to God — exalted is He — at the moment of the preacher's supplication upon the pulpit, and sets his resolve upon something in his mind, he attains it, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And when "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" is recited for love over a cup of water, the aforementioned number of times as has preceded, and he gives that water to drink, that person will love him with an intense love — and especially if it be within what is lawful. And if some of that water is given to drink to one dull of mind at the rising of the sun over a period of days, the dullness that was in him departs from him, and he retains everything he hears, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And when it is recited at the falling of rain 61 times with the intention of seeking rain for whatever place on the earth it may be, God — exalted is He — waters it that day; and even

— even were the reciter in the East and the place he intends in the West. And if "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" is recited after the dawn prayer with a truthful intention and a humbled heart for a period of 40 days, God, exalted is He, pours out upon his heart the abstruse depths of the secrets, and he sees in his sleep everything that comes to pass in the world. As for the number of its recitation, it is 2,500 times every day; and he must keep constantly to the discipline (riyāḍa) of abstaining from every ensouled creature and from whatever issues from an ensouled creature. Then he will see a wonder. Let him keep his secret hidden, and he will attain his desire.

Know, my brother — may God grant us and you success in obeying Him — that I have made this basmala and its occult properties plain only so that profit may be had from it in obedience to God, exalted is He; and I have against you a guarantor and a surety. So, if you wish to operate with it for the accomplishing of needs and for gaining access to kings, then fast on Thursday, and break your fast only with oil or with dates. You pray the sunset prayer and recite it 121 times; and when you take to your bed you recite it without count until sleep overcomes you. Then, when you rise on the morning of Friday, pray the dawn prayer and recite it the number [prescribed] at the first sunset prayer. You write it on paper (kāghad) with musk, saffron, and rose-water, and you suffumigate it with aloeswood and ambergris; and the writing of it is the number mentioned. By God, no man or woman has ever carried that writing but that he became, in the eyes of the people, like the shining moon; he was mighty, awe-inspiring, of high standing, obeyed, and honoured; everyone who saw him loved him and granted him his need, and awe of him and love of him were cast into the hearts of all creatures.
This is the form mentioned. You also write it in this form:

. You write it 21 times. And if he writes it in joined Arabic script, that is another method, according to what we mentioned first: you write it thus —. You write it on gazelle parchment 151 times with saffron and rose-water, and you suffumigate it with costus (qusṭ), storax (mayʿa), and benzoin (jāwī). If one whose provision has been straitened carries it, that [straitness] departs from him and God, exalted is He, opens to him the door of good. No debtor has ever carried this slip but that God, /fol. 30v./ exalted is He, discharged his debt; and it was for him a safeguard from every evil and every ill.

And if he writes it in a glass bowl 40 times and you wash it off with the water of Zamzam or the water of a sweet well, and a sick man drinks of that water, God, exalted is He, restores him to health. And if a woman whose delivery has become difficult drinks of that water, she gives birth on the instant, by the leave of God, exalted is He, [the child] safe from every ill and sound. And if the basmala is written on a sheet 35 times and you hang it in the house, no devil and no jinnī enters it, and blessing grows abundant in his dwelling and his wealth. And if that sheet, or the like of it, is hung in a shop, its customers grow many, its profit increases, its merchandise and its wares sell briskly, and God, exalted is He, blinds the eyes of the wrongdoers to it — all this through the blessing of the basmala and the blessing of God, exalted is He. And if it is written on the first day of Muḥarram upon a sheet 113 times and a person carries it from that [day], no ill and no hateful thing shall reach him, neither him nor the people of his house, for the whole span of his life. And if it is written on a sheet for the miqlāt woman — she being the one whose child does not live — and likewise for the barren woman who has not yet conceived, after a purification of 3 days; and the sheet is placed upon her, its number being the same as what has preceded; and her husband the man has intercourse with her: she conceives by him, by the leave of God, exalted is He. She must not part from the writing that is upon her for 61 days; and after that, if she wishes she may lay the writing aside, and if she wishes she may keep it fastened upon her. A child will come to her in whom there is good, and she will never feel pain or hardship in the carrying of it. In some copies, the writing of the basmala is 61 times, and that is the more correct. And God knows best. So likewise is the sheet of the miqlāt woman: if she does the like of that and then carries it, her child lives, by the leave of God, exalted is He. This has been tried again and again, and all of it proved true — together with truthfulness of intention.

And if "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" is written upon a white sheet 101 times, and it is buried in the sown field, its cultivation prospers, it is secured from all blights, it grows, blessing enters into it, it comes out sound, and he attains in it his desire, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if the basmala is written 70 times and placed with the dead man in his shroud, he is secured from the terror of Munkar and Nakīr, and it is a light for him until the Day of the Raising, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if it is written upon a tablet of black lead 3 times and he puts it in the net of a fisher of fish, the fish gather to him, by the leave of God, exalted is He, from every place, and he catches of them what he wishes, through the blessing of God, exalted is He, and the blessing of this noble and mighty Name — for it is the most beloved of the names of God, exalted is He, to Him. And if you write a slip once and place it beneath the bezel of a ring, and that ring is put into churned milk, and one who has been stung drinks it and vomits it up, the poison comes out, if God, exalted is He, wills, and he is cured of the pain he suffers, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if it is written with the letters disjoined, thus, and he carries it, it has a mighty excellence; and this is its form:
understand.

Know that the bāʾ is the splendour (bahāʾ) of God, exalted is He; the sīn, His sublimity (sanāʾ); the mīm, His glory and His dominion; the alif, His eternity without beginning; /fol. 31r./ the lām, His subtle kindness; the hāʾ, "He is God, there is no god but He"; the alif, His command; the lām, "to Him belongs the kingdom"; the ḥāʾ, "Living, Everlasting"; the rāʾ, "Ever-Gentle, Compassionate"; the mīm, His kingdom; and the nūn, His favour. And if you write from the basmala thethus, 21 times, and the basmala is recited over it with a truthful intention 100 times, and you place it among his wealth, the blessing in it increases and it grows, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if you write it thus 20 times, and he adds to it these letters, which are as you see —

[ that is, Peace be upon Noah among all beings (Q 37:79)] — and gives it as a drink to the one who has been stung, it heals him of the pain he suffers, and God, exalted is He, restores him to health. And if it is written upon a sheet and he looks at the letter mīm 40 times each day, saying: Say: O God, Master of all dominion, You give dominion to whom You will and You strip dominion from whom

You will; You exalt whom You will and You abase whom You will. In Your hand is [all] good; truly You are powerful over everything. You make the night pass into the day and You make the day pass into the night; You bring forth the living from the dead and You bring forth the dead from the living; and You provide for whom You will, without reckoning (Q 3:26–27) — and he carries it, he will not know from what quarter good comes to him. And if you write al-Raḥmān (the All-Merciful) 50 times upon a sheet on which "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" stands 150 times, and you carry it and go in upon the sultan, or upon a man who is a wrongdoer or a tyrant, you are safe from his evil, and no ill and no hateful thing shall reach you. And if the basmala is written every day 1,000 times with a truthful intention and a humbled heart, after fasting and discipline and ritual purity, and that continues for 14 days — and in another transmission, if it is written after each prayer 1,000 times for the period mentioned — then he beholds all the angels, and they speak to him and he speaks to them; they serve him and are at his disposal in all his affairs; he deploys them throughout the world and they obey him in everything he wishes and aims at, if God, exalted is He, wills. And if he writes it broken, thus, in disjoined letters — —and you also write the name of the one you desire and the name of his mother, both broken, and you break them and spread them and carry them with you at a fortunate hour in which you meet that person, then, when he looks at you, he grants your need; and were you to command him to cast himself into the fire, he would do it. And if you write al-Raḥmān thus — [ — a number of] times, and you also write the name of your servant who is much given to running away, and you bury that writing in the house and weigh it down with a stone, after you say: "O God, I ask You by the right of 'In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate,' and I ask You by the right of Your name al-Raḥmān, that You restrain this servant from running away, O Lord of all beings" — then he repents of flight, by the leave of God, exalted is He; he will not go out of the house he is in, and he will not run away at all. And if you write al-Raḥmān upon a steel knife whose blade is of one piece with it, and you recite over it what you have written 331 times, and you slaughter a cock with it and sever its head from its body, it walks without a head. Then, after that, you take the head of the cock and bury it beneath the threshold of the house, and all the noxious vermin flee from it, and likewise all the jinn. And if the head of that cock is fried /fol. 31v./ in good oil and you set that oil aside, that oil gives great benefit, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if a woman applies it upon a wad of cotton, and she suffers from haemorrhage, it benefits her, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if you write al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate) 299 times and carry that writing and enter into the fray of battle, no weapon shall work upon you, no harm shall befall you, and everyone who meets you shall flee from before you, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if al-Raḥīm is written upon a sheet 21 times and hung upon one afflicted with headache, it departs from him, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if you write His name al-Raḥīm upon the palm of one seized by a fit (maṣrūʿ) and speak it into his ear 7 times, he comes to himself on the instant, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if you write the blessed Name al-Raḥīm upon 7 almond kernels with a needle of brass on Friday in the hour of Venus — which is the first hour, at the rising of the sun — and if you write the noble Name according to its number upon those almonds and feed them to the one you desire, he will love you with a love so intense that there is no increasing upon it. And if you write the name al-Raḥīm in this form [figure not reproduced in the edition]. And if it is written upon a piece of leopard-skin or cheetah-skin and one faint of heart carries it, his heart is emboldened and his resolve strengthened, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if you write His name al-Raḥīm thus [figure not reproduced in the edition]. And if it is written upon a new mirror on Monday at the rising of the sun and one afflicted with facial palsy (al-laqwa) gazes into it much, God, exalted is He, cures him of it. And if he writes it thus — al-Raḥīm — in this form: — upon a ring

— of silver, its weight two dirhams: God, exalted is He, bestows upon its bearer love, awe, and obedience, by the leave of God, blessed and exalted. And this is the form of the signet, and it is as you see.

And for the cutting off of tyrants and the arrogant: write the table of the basmala on a piece of lead, and place the name of the person sought, as mentioned, in the table of the signet; suffumigate it with asafoetida (ḥiltīt) and red garlic; then bury the signet in a place close beside a fire that burns perpetually. And beware of letting the fire reach the lead, for then the one against whom that is done perishes and dies, and you are the one answerable for him on the Day of Resurrection. This is its form. And these are the names which you say over the aforementioned signet: O God, I ask You by the right of Your mighty Name, which is "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", before which faces are humbled, to which necks bow down, before which voices are hushed, and in dread of which hearts quake — I ask You to bless /fol. 32r./ and grant peace to our master Muḥammad, and to his family and his companions, and to grant peace; and that You fulfil my need concerning So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]. O God, if You know that he will turn back from that which he is in, then guide him and grant him success; and if You know that he will not turn back from that which he is in, then send down upon him Your affliction, Your wrath, and Your displeasure, and destroy him — O al-Qāhir (the Subduer), O al-Qahhār (the All-Subduing), O al-Qādir (the Powerful), O al-Muqtadir (the Omnipotent), O God, O God — seven times. And you make this invocation seven hundred times; for the one against whom it is done, God destroys him or guides him. So fear God, exalted is He. And God is the granter of success in what is right.

And if you write the noble basmala, as I shall draw it for you, in the middle of a circle, and write within the circle and around it Muḥammad is the Messenger of God; and those who are with him are severe against the unbelievers (Q 48:29) to the end of the sura, and suffumigate it with everything of sweet fragrance at an auspicious time, and carry it — then you become awe-inspiring, magnified, and honoured in the sight of everyone; and none sees you but he loves you and seeks your company and your companionship, so much so that women incline toward you and toward intimacy with you. So fear God, exalted is He, in secret and in the open. And God is the granter of success. And this is the form of the circle, and it is as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided.

And if you write the basmala in its entirety — the moon being in Pisces and the ascendant auspicious — upon gazelle parchment, and he carries it with him after he has recited it over the parchment to the count of its number: then if he lives, he lives happy, and if he dies, he dies a martyr, and he will never see anything hateful befall him, through the blessing of the noble basmala.

Know, O you — may God grant me and you success in obedience to Him — that bism is the concealed Name; that Allāh, exalted is He, is the Greatest Name; and that by al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm He describes Himself, for He is the All-Merciful of this world and the Compassionate of the hereafter. And al-ḥamdu li-llāhi rabbi l-ʿālamīn ("Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds") stands opposite "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate": so bism Allāh stands opposite al-ḥamdu li-llāh; rabb stands opposite al-Raḥmān; al-ʿālamīn stands opposite al-Raḥīm. And know that all of that is taken into account in His saying Master of the Day of Judgement (Q 1:4) — by "Judgement" He intends the manifestation of Lordship. So He is Malik (King) and Mālik (Master) and Malīk (Sovereign): by the illumination of the intellects and of the subtle lights on the Day of Judgement with the attribute of kingship, so that He is Malik; and He manifests Himself to the souls with subjugating power and dominion, so that He is Mālik yawm al-dīn (Master of the Day of Judgement); and He manifests Himself to those possessed of mercy in the worldly abode by way of possession, so that He is Mālik al-mulūk (Master of kings); and He manifests Himself to those brought near by way of al-Malīk, according to His saying, exalted is He: in a seat of truthfulness, with a Sovereign Omnipotent (Q 54:55).

So understand the secret of these divine subtleties. And all of this is within "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". The bāʾ that is in the Name serves to convey the good from all the worlds to the True King, and it raises up the call by the tongue through the instrument of utterance. So bism Allāh is an ascent that has no limit, and al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm is a descent to the final issue, just as bism Allāh is a rising up to the First Beginning. In it, then, is the secret of the beginning and of the end; and in it are the degrees of the affirmation of divine unity, because bism stands opposite shahida ("[God] bears witness"), and Allāh opposite Allāh, and "the angels" opposite al-Raḥmān, and "those possessed of knowledge" opposite al-Raḥīm. And likewise by relation to the quadratic world, which is His saying, exalted is He: Those are with those whom God has favoured — of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous (Q 4:69). "The prophets" is a relation from bism to Allāh; "and the truthful" is a relation from Allāh to bism, which are the degrees of the prophets; "the martyrs", from All-Mercifulness (raḥmāniyya) to Compassionateness (raḥīmiyya); and "the righteous", from Compassionateness to All-Mercifulness. That, then, is the succession of the steps in the ascent to the secret of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". For the beginning of the circle of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" is like its end, and its inward like its outward. By it God set up the tree of the created beings, and by it He made manifest the secret of engendering, and how the worlds became separated out from "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate".

And in the noble hadith: ((Whoever comes on the Day of Resurrection with "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" in his scroll eight hundred and twelve times — and that is the number of the letters of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" after the dropping of their repetitions, their number being four hundred and six, and its double, eight hundred and twelve times — and is a believer, certain of His Lordship, God frees him from the Fire and admits him into the Garden, the abode of permanence.)) Then God, blessed and exalted, said to Jesus son of Mary — peace be upon him: ((O Jesus, let "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" be at the opening of your recitation and of your prayers; for whoever sets it at the opening of his recitation and his prayer, neither Munkar nor Nakīr shall terrify him. And if he dies upon that, God makes light for him the agonies of death and the narrowness of the grave, and the mercy of God is /fol. 33r./ upon him; and He makes his grave spacious for him, and illumines it for him as far as his sight can reach, and brings him forth from his grave on the Day of Resurrection with body made white, his face gleaming with light; and He reckons with him an easy reckoning, and makes his balance heavy, and grants him the perfect light upon the Bridge (al-ṣirāṭ) until he enters the Garden; and He commands the herald to call out over him in the open courts of the Resurrection with happiness and forgiveness. Jesus — peace be upon him — said: O Lord, is this for me alone? He said: It is for you and for whoever follows you in particular, and takes as you take and speaks as you speak; and that shall belong to Aḥmad and to his community after you.))

So Jesus — peace be upon him — informed his companions of that. And when Jesus — peace be upon him — was raised up to heaven, the disciples passed away and others came after them, and they went astray and led astray, and altered and substituted, and exchanged religion for this world. So the verse of faith was taken away from the breasts of the Christians and the monks, and it remained in the breasts of the people of the Gospel, until God, exalted is He, sent our Prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — and sent it down upon him in Sūrat al-Naml, and it was an opening. And the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — gave command, and it was written at the heads of the suras and of the registers and at the heads of letters. And the Lord of Might swore by His might that no believing servant should pronounce it over anything without His blessing it for him.

And it is related from the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — that he said: ((Whoever recites "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" and is a believer, the mountains and the celestial spheres glorify God together with him, save that he does not hear their glorification.)) And the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace —

said: ((When the believing servant says "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", the Garden says: At Your service, and at Your good pleasure! O God, Your servant So-and-so has said "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate"; O God, draw him far away from the Fire and admit him into Your Garden.)) And it is related from the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — that he said: ((There are among my community a people who will come on the Day of Resurrection saying "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", and their good deeds will weigh heavier than their evil deeds.)) And the nations will say: Glory be to God! How the good deeds of the community of Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — outweigh! And their prophets will say to them: It is only the Name of God, exalted is He, that has come to them. And that is because the beginning of their speech was three of the mighty names of God, exalted is He — were they set in one pan of a balance, and the heavens and the earths and all that is in them and all that is between them set in the second pan, they would outweigh them — and they are "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". Then he said: ((And He has made it a security against every affliction, a remedy for every malady, and a protective charm against every accursed satan. And this community has been made safe from being swallowed up by the earth, from being pelted, from metamorphosis, and from drowning, through its blessing. So hold fast to reciting it, and draw near by means of it to the Possessor of Majesty and Honour.))

And al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said concerning His saying, exalted is He, And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qurʾān, they turn away upon their backs, recoiling (Q 17:46): he said, that means [their recoiling] from "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". And it has been said concerning His saying, exalted is He, And He bound them to the word of pious reverence (kalimat al-taqwā), and they had the better right to it and were its rightful people (Q 48:26), that it was "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". And whoever writes it /fol. 33v./ and writes it finely, in reverence for it, is recorded with God among those brought near.

And it is related from ʿIkrima that he said: ((God, exalted is He, was, and nothing was with Him. Then He created the creation of the light; then from the light He created the Tablet and the Pen. Then God, exalted is He, commanded the Pen to run over the Tablet with all that would come to be until the Day of Resurrection. And the first thing the Pen wrote upon the Preserved Tablet was "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". So He made it a security for His creation so long as they hold to reciting it; and it is the recitation of the people of the seven heavens and of the people of the pavilions of glory among the angels — the cherubim, those ranged in ranks, and those who glorify. And the first thing that was sent down upon Adam — peace be upon him — was this verse, which is "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". And he said: I have come to know that my believing progeny will not be chastised with the Fire so long as they hold to it. Then it was taken up after him, until the time of the Friend [of God], Abraham — peace be upon him — and it was sent down upon him while he was in the mangonel, and God, exalted is He, delivered him by it from the fire. Then it was taken up after him, until the time of Solomon son of David — peace be upon them both — and it was sent down upon him; and the angels said: Now has God completed your kingdom, O Solomon son of David! And God, exalted is He, commanded him to proclaim among all the tribes (asbāṭ), the ascetics, and the devotees: Lo, whoever wishes to hear the verse of security, let him gather to Solomon son of David — peace be upon him — in the prayer-niche of his father. So they gathered to him, and Solomon — peace be upon him — arose and ascended the pulpit and recited to them the verse of security — and in some copies, the verse of faith — and it is "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". And when they had learned it they came forward rejoicing and said: We bear witness that you are truly the Messenger of God, O son of David. Then it was taken up after him, until the time of Moses — peace be upon him — and it was sent down upon him; and by it he subdued Pharaoh and his hosts, and Qārūn and his hosts and his partisans, and Hāmān and his partisans. Then it was taken up after Moses, until the time of Jesus — peace be upon him. And God revealed to him, saying: O son of Mary, do you not know what verse has been sent down upon you? He said: Yes indeed, O Lord. He said to him: O Jesus, there has been sent down upon you the verse of security — and it is said, the verse of faith — and it is "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". So hold fast to reciting it in your night and your day, in your going forth at morning and your coming, in your sitting and your standing, in your eating and your drinking, and in all your states. For whoever comes on the Day of Resurrection with eight hundred and twelve times of it in his scroll — and the hadith has already been given.

And it is related of one of the righteous that he came to one of the friends of God (awliyāʾ) to visit him and to seek his supplication and his blessing. He found the people gathered at his door, awaiting his coming out; and a rainbow (qaws quzaḥ) was set upright over his door. While things were thus, behold, the master had opened the door and come out. Then he set his foot upon the rainbow and said "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", and passed over it and walked on until he came down on the other side, while the people looked at him and marvelled at him. Then the man who had come to visit him — he was called al-Shaykh al-Malījī — when he saw what the master did, said: Alas! /fol. 34r./ And he was stirred, and said: Thus do [true] men outstrip [others]; and thus shall we be, if God, exalted is He, wills. Then the shaykh [al-Malījī] set himself to earnestness and striving until he joined the solitary ones (al-afrād). And the man who passed over the aforementioned rainbow was Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Rajrājī — may God be pleased with him.
So look, my brother, at what is in "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate"; and listen, and lend both your ears to the saying of

God, exalted is He: It is from Solomon, and it is: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Do not exalt yourselves above me, but come to me in submission (Q 27:30–31) — how Bilqīs became obedient to Solomon, and faith entered her heart, and this came about through the blessing of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". And in it, of secrets and acts, of the attracting of hearts and bodies, and of that whereby hearts are gladdened and souls are made to rejoice, there is a wondrous matter. And know, my brother, that "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" is nineteen letters, as has already been stated. In it are ten that are unrepeated, and they are:(bāʾ),(sīn),(mīm),(alif),(lām),(hāʾ), (rāʾ), (nūn),(yāʾ). In it the mīm is repeated three times, the lām (ḥāʾ), four times, the rāʾ twice, and the ḥāʾ 2 times; the bāʾ is not repeated, nor the nūn, nor the yāʾ likewise, nor the hāʾ, nor the sīn likewise. And the repeated among them are five letters, and they are these:. Of these the mīm is repeated in it 3 times, and the alif likewise, and the lām four times, and the rāʾ twice, and the ḥāʾ 2 times. So it results from this that the root of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" is ten unrepeated letters. Among them is the bāʾ, which serves to convey the good; and it is a cold letter, and therefore I always begin with it in the verse of security. And the letter bāʾ is among the letters that remain on the Day of Resurrection, and it is a hidden secret. That is because the odd (al-witr) is the secret of the indications in respect of the Essence, save that it is an indication of the Reality, and it is from you to Him.

And know that it stands at the head of the scrolls of Abraham — peace be upon him — these names, which are "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate"; and likewise in the scroll of Noah — peace be upon him; and likewise in the scroll of Solomon son of David — peace be upon him. Then likewise at the beginning of the revelation to the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — in His saying, exalted is He: Recite in the name of your Lord, who created man from a clot (Q 96:1–2). So He began with the secret of the bāʾ, which conceals the secrets of the divine realities. It is from you to Him, and they are the concealed contents of the Essence, by the secret of self-disclosure (tajallī), according to His saying: "Through Me you have known Me". And when He created the bāʾ, He created together with it eighty-one angels, who glorify God, exalted is He, and hallow Him.

And among the occult properties of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" is that the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((Whoever says, when he rises in the morning, three times: "In the name of God the Mighty, with whose Name nothing in the earth or in heaven can do harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing" — no sudden calamity and no affliction shall befall him until evening; and whoever says it when evening comes, three times, no sudden calamity and no affliction shall befall him until morning. And in one transmission: no paralysis shall befall him; and in another transmission: nothing shall befall him.)) And so Khālid ibn al-Walīd — may God be pleased with him — came to the poison and drank it down. That was when the great one of the Byzantines — that is, the king of the Christians — sent to him and said to him: If you are truthful in what you say, that poison does no harm together with these words, then drink it. He said: So our master Khālid — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — took the poison in the presence of the envoy whom he had sent, and in the presence of a company of the Companions and others, and placed it in his palm and said: "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate"; "In the name of God, with whose Name nothing in the earth or in heaven can do harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." Then he drank it down, and it did him no harm at all, save that he broke out in a sweat, by the leave of God, exalted is He. So look at this gracious Name, and how it wards off poison. And by this noble Name /fol. 34v./ the ark of Noah — peace be upon him — ran its course, and he was delivered, through His saying, exalted is He: In the name of God is its sailing and its anchoring (Q 11:41). And by it God, exalted is He, delivered the Friend [of God], Abraham — peace be upon him — from the fire of Nimrod, and God, exalted is He, made it coolness and peace for him. And by it is deliverance when you enter your house and when you go out, according to his saying — upon him be blessing and peace: ((And say, when you enter your house and when you go out: "In the name of God we have entered, in the name of God we have gone out, and upon God we rely." And you say it also at the shutting of the doors; for Satan does not open a lock over which the Name of God, exalted is He, is invoked, nor does he come near it.)) And among its occult properties is that, when you go to your bed, you say: "In the name of God, and upon the religion of the

Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace." And the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((There is no ablution for him who does not pronounce the Name.)) And from Abū Dāwūd: ((And whoever eats with a leper and says "In the name of God, in trust in God and in reliance upon Him", nothing shall harm him.)) And ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb — may God be pleased with him — did this with Muʿayqīb al-Dawsī, who was a leper, when the food was brought to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb — may God be pleased with him — and he was present. ʿUmar — may God be pleased with him — said to him: Eat with us. "In the name of God, in trust in God and in reliance upon Him." So he drew near and ate with him.

And by this noble Name healing is sought from the evil eye: you strike with your hand upon the breast of the one struck by the eye and say: "In the name of God; O God, take away its heat and its sickness." And you say it when a man sets his foot in the stirrup intending to travel: he says "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", and no hateful thing shall ever reach him. And when the believing servant says "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", Satan shrinks until he becomes like a fly. And the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — used to say it to whoever went forth as a traveller and to whom he wished to bid farewell; and he would say, when he mounted: ((In the name of God, and by God, and upon the religion of the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace.)) And with it the Messenger of God used to make his opening upon his journey, saying: ((In the name of God; I take refuge with God from the hardship of travel, from a sight that brings gloom, and from an evil return in respect of family, property, and child.)) And the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said to Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, when his hand was struck and his fingers were cut off: ((Truly, had you said "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", the angels would have raised you up while the people looked on.))

So consider this Name, which the angels raise up — that is, the one who utters it; and at whose mention the satans shrink; and at whose mention poison is cut off. The lord of mankind has made known to you its worth, and the Lord of the Throne has granted you its secret and its excellence — so wherever you seek it, you find it — and its glory. So make no movement and keep no stillness save with its mention; for by it you are given provision, and made happy, and kept safe, and delivered. And all of that is folded within "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". And with "In the name of God" Jesus — peace be upon him — used to perform healing recitation (ruqya) and have it performed against pains and against every kind of harm.

And some of the masters said: whoever writes the form of the bāʾ on a Friday, having fasted on the Thursday and given alms, and hangs it upon his right upper arm — God, exalted is He, expands his breast, removes sloth from him, makes blessing manifest upon him, shows him the secret of the bāʾ that subsists by it, and he sees the lights of the angels when their forms appear, the celestial and the terrestrial. It appears as an upright form, perfect in shape, sweet of scent; the noble ones among the great ones see that, save that it speaks with the bāʾ, and it is fixed in light, its light does not change. And when the name of the bāʾ is invoked, its light appears upon its essence. And it is one of /fol. 35r./ the treasured Names. And this letter, when it is in one of the names of God, exalted is He, and someone invokes it, he is treated with kindness. And it is fitting that the name containing the bāʾ be written for every dry pain and for every difficult matter, for God makes that matter easy. And it is among the names of God, exalted is He: in His name, exalted is He, al-Barr (the Benign), al-Bāriʾ (the Maker), al-Bāqī (the Abiding), and al-Bāʿith (the Raiser of the dead); and in them is the secret of subsistence (baqāʾ). For that reason God, exalted is He, bestowed it as a favour within "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". That is because the upright alif is the head of the bāʾ, and it is the outspread one that has spread out within the essence of the bāʾ — thus:.And the bāʾ has appeared also in His name al-Baṣīr (the All-Seeing), and in His name al-Badīʿ (the Wondrous Originator), and in His name al-Bāṭin (the Hidden). In every name there is a meaning proper to it: thus al-Barr is for the people of piety (birr), aiding in the works of piety and in filial devotion to parents.

And whoever mentions it two hundred and thirty-three times every day, after he has mixed it with the name of the one to whom he wishes to show kindness — and that is, that you take, for example, the name ʿAmr, thus:; then you take the first letter from the name al-Barr and set it at the head of the first line; then you take the first letter from the name ʿAmr and set it after it, thus, to the end of the two names, thus:
. Then you take it and break it (taksīr) until the two names come back and appear as they were the first time, thus:
