The figure: the first [line] has come round last. Drop the last, and there remain four mixed lines. Write them upon whatever you wish, and put them in your bosom, and speak over them with this speech, saying: O Lord of lords, Nurturer of all, by the subtlety of Your Lordship hasten to me a flowing forth of Your subtlety, that I may be drowned in a sea from among the seas of Your power and rejoice in the sweetness of that sea — a sweetness that makes sweet the spirits of those who find rest in the understanding of Your secrets. And grant me a name from among the names of Your power, such that whoever arms himself with it is guarded from the evil of what He has scattered abroad in the earth, and the evil of what comes forth from it, and of what descends from heaven and what ascends therein. Truly You are al-Laṭīf (the Subtle), al-Ḥafīẓ (the Preserver), al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing). And as for His name al-Bāriʾ (the Maker), it is for the healing (ibrāʾ) of pains and sicknesses; and as for al-Bāqī (the Everlasting) and al-Bāʿith (the Raiser of the dead), they have occult properties which will come in their proper places, if God, exalted is He, wills.

Let us now return to what we were about and engaged upon. As for the letter sīn: when God, exalted is He, created it from the world of His command, He sent down with it nine thousand eight hundred and thirty angels. It is the first letter that received from the bāʾ the secret of its bringing-into-being, and it is one of the letters of the outward aspect of the Greatest Name. Now the Greatest Name has an outward and an inward: by its outward the heavens were established, and by its inward were established the things of the upper world — the Footstool and the Throne. For that reason the sīn falls at the beginning of al-samāwāt (the heavens) and in the third rank of al-kursī (the Footstool). And since the bāʾ is attached to power — and it is the concealed of the concealed things — and the hāʾ, because the hāʾ is from you to Him /fol. 35v./: so you say Huwa Huwa ("He, He"), and He says bī bī ("by Me, by Me"). And in Sūrat Yā-Sīn there are names from among the names of wisdom. Whoever lights upon them and writes them and effaces them with pure water, facing the qibla, for as many days as the number of the names — God, exalted is He, causes him to speak with wisdom. And it is the middle of the sura, and the number of its letters is sixteen letters, of which two letters are dotted above and two letters dotted below; and it is five words, the first of which is the letter sīn and the last the letter mīm. And this letter has appeared in His name al-Salām (the Peace), His name al-Samīʿ (the All-Hearing), and His name al-Sarīʿ (the Swift). Al-Samīʿ is the name of those who are insistent in supplication especially, for often the answer comes swiftly to him; and likewise al-Sarīʿ: whoever mentions it and asks for an answer obtains it. And whoever desires some need of God, exalted is He, that he may attain it, let him inscribe it upon his two palms and raise them up and make entreaty by the name, multiplied by the days, and let him bring its number to the full; for the answer will come to him from God, exalted is He, after the aforementioned count. And its number multiplied by the days is four thousand two hundred and seventy-seven. And whoever desires the vision of the spirits, let him make entreaty by it to God, exalted is He, that He unveil for him the eye of certainty; then he will speak with them and ask about what he wishes, and they will answer him. In it are hidden secrets and manifest operations. So search out and operate: you will arrive and attain. As for His name al-Samīʿ: whoever adjoins to it al-Baṣīr (the All-Seeing) and says "Yā Samīʿ, yā Baṣīr", and writes them at a favourable time, and casts the writing upon one who has fainted — he comes to at once. And this has been beheld with their own eyes by the masters of the secrets; for when they came to it they found at its gate

Ibrāhīm b. Jārūkh, who had fallen into a swoon. So the wafq was inscribed for him and cast upon him, after the two names had been recited seven hundred and fifty-four times; and he came to, and what he was suffering departed from him, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if the two are inscribed upon gold and a person carries them, he hears the tongues of the jinn and sees them, and he exercises authority over the spirits in whatever he wishes. And if he persists in the litany of remembrance by means of them, he is granted unveiling of the secrets of created beings, and he informs them of what is in their inmost thoughts, and the states of all the servants become manifest to him. And this has been witnessed many times. As for His name al-Salām: it is for the seeking of safety and the seeking of security. And it is the litany of remembrance of our master the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — on the Day of Resurrection and on the day his community passes over the Bridge (al-ṣirāṭ); he says: "Yā Salām, sallim" (O Peace, grant safety!). And in another transmission, that he — God bless him and grant him peace — says: "Sallim, yā Salām" (Grant safety, O Peace!).

As for the letter mīm of bism: the mīm is one of the diameters (aqṭār) of the letters; and the diameters of the letters are every letter whose beginning is like its end, namely the wāw, the mīm, and the nūn. And the mīm points to gathering, because of the encompassment it contains, and it points to stillness, because of the awe it contains. It is one of the letters of the Tablet. And when God, exalted is He, created it, He created it as a light /fol. 36r./, round, blotted out with light. And it is one of the letters of the intellect, because of its encompassing; and from it the sun in the fourth sphere draws its sustaining supply. And by its secret God, exalted is He, established the kingdom and the dominion; and the manifestation of knowledge is by the mīm, so that it is an aid in the operations, by the secret of the light of the mīm. And it is the last rank of bism. In it is the secret of the attainment of full strength, according to His saying, exalted is He: until, when he reaches his full strength and reaches forty years (Q 46:15). And the numbers that fall to the mīm are forty. And God, exalted is He, has appointed over it ninety angels from among the angels of the Tablet. And it is the secret which God, exalted is He, deposited in the name of His Prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — at its beginning, and that by the secret of the dominion (malakūt); and in its middle, by the secret of the kingdom (mulk). There is gathered for him the innermost reality of the world of dominion and the world of the kingdom. So whoever gazes upon the form of the mīm forty times every day while reciting His saying, exalted is He, Say: O God, Master of the kingdom, You give the kingdom to whom You will— up to His saying, exalted is He — without reckoning (Q 3:26–27) — God, exalted is He, will make easy for him the means of this world and of the hereafter. That is to say, the eightfold figure (al-muthamman), the description of which and the discussion of which will come; and it belongs to Mercury, on Wednesday. So whoever inscribes its numerical secret — after fasting forty days, maintaining ritual purity continuously, and the remembrance of God, exalted is He

— upon pure parchment, facing the qibla, in the purity of the complete ablution, the moon being in Saʿd al-Suʿūd and the hour being that of the sun: then no blameworthy thought will occur to its bearer, and God, exalted is He, will grant him an opening through the reception of the realities of faith and the holy lights. And the one who wears it is secure from every harm, and God, exalted is He, bestows awe upon him. And whoever supplicates by it on Friday, while fasting and constant in the litany of remembrance, and supplicates by it concerning a righteous need — God, exalted is He, fulfils his need. And likewise whoever carries it while he is engaged in pursuing his means of livelihood — God multiplies his good, and God, exalted is He, makes easy the means of his provision and provides for him whence he does not reckon. And in it also there is, of the joining of hearts and their inclining and their turning toward the one who seeks them, that which is a blessing and more, for whoever contemplates them and to whom God, exalted is He, has given understanding of its secret. And its figuration and its representation will come in its proper place, when the discussion of it arrives. And the manner of supplicating by it for a need is that you gather, from the Most Beautiful Names of God, exalted is He, all its numbers, as I shall represent it for you together with its figures; and I shall expound to you how you may draw hearts to you, and their affection toward you, and their turning about in the phases of love for you, and their submission to you — such as you will not find in any book, nor light upon in any register. So take care to keep it hidden and to guard it, for it is the red sulphur, the greatest treasure, and the most renowned magnet.

And know, O my brother, that whoever has been granted an opening onto the secrets of the mīm, its encompassing, its closing round upon itself, and the worlds it contains, has witnessed the wonders of the engendered worlds. And likewise whoever wishes God, exalted is He, to make memorization easy for him: let him write this numerical secret on Thursday, in a state of purity, facing the qibla /fol. 36v./, and with it the name of the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — forty times; then let him efface it and drink it with water and bees' honey, and say: O God, by the blessing of what I have drunk, make memorization and understanding easy for me. And let him persist in that for forty days: God will grant him an opening, outwardly and inwardly. This is for whoever understands the secret of the mīm, until he beholds what is in the power of its inward, of every world, in the secret by which He established the mīm. By this aspiration the opening comes. As for its literal figure, it is among the treasured secrets. And that is: whoever writes it upon pure parchment on Monday, in the hour of the moon, and suffumigates it with storax (aṣṭarak), and conceals some matter within himself and wishes to see its outcome, and fasts that day of his purely for God, exalted is He — and let him break his fast upon a little bread, and let him perform his litany (wird), and let him sleep in the purity of the ablution, and let him sleep upon his right side, and let him recite Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion (Q 67:1) with it beneath his head, and let him not speak with anyone after it, and let him sleep — then God, exalted is He, will apprise him of the outcome of his affair according to the measure of the portion he intended. And that is fitting only for the people of purity of hearts and bodies and the people of spiritual discipline (riyāḍa). And likewise whoever writes it in a glass cup and drinks it — God, exalted is He, makes wisdom easy for him. And whoever hangs it upon himself — God, exalted is He, makes understanding easy for him and causes him to speak with wisdom. And whoever writes it, and with it lā ilāha illā Allāh ("There is no god but God") eighty times, and hangs it upon his right upper arm, or writes it upon a garment and wears that garment — God, exalted is He, bestows upon him awe and compassion.

And if he keeps to a single unbroken course and practises spiritual discipline, there is no doubt that God, exalted is He, will apprise him of the world of the jinn, after you write what I describe to you. And likewise, if you wish to take brethren from among the believing jinn who will fulfil your need for you and strive for your good pleasure, you begin with the fast on Wednesday until

— Saturday, the fourth day of it, after you have performed the full ablution (ghusl); and you wash your clothes on each day of these days — I mean, you perform the full ablution, since the full ablution is indispensable. And you recite Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ1,000 times, and Sūrat Yā-Sīn once, and Sūrat al-Dukhān likewise, and Tanzīl al-Sajda (Sūrat al-Sajda) and Tabāraka lladhī bi-yadihi l-mulk (Sūrat al-Mulk), once. Then, when it is the afternoon of Saturday — and that is the tenth [hour] — you withdraw from people in a pure and empty place, in a clean spot, and you take seven warrants (barāwāt) of paper (kāghad). And you write upon the first His saying, exalted is He: And He it is who gives life and gives death — to His saying — the day (Q 23:80); and His saying, exalted is He: And when He has decreed a matter, He but says to it "Be", and it is (Q 2:117); God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). And you write upon the second His saying, exalted is He: Truly your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then mounted the Throne — to His saying, exalted is He — so blessed be God, the Lord of the worlds (Q 7:54); and His saying, exalted is He: /fol. 37r./ and He has encompassed everything in knowledge (Q 65:12), and He has numbered everything in counting (Q 72:28), God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). And you write upon the third: and a messenger to the Children of Israel — to His saying — by the leave of God (Q 3:49); God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). And you write upon the fourth: Then, when He calls you with a single call from the earth, at once you come forth (Q 30:25); God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). And you write upon the fifth: and at once they are hastening forth from the graves to their Lord (Q 36:51); God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). And you write upon the sixth: And the Trumpet is blown, and at once they are standing, looking on (Q 39:68); God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). And you write upon the seventh: On the day when they come forth from the graves in haste, as though they were racing toward a standard set up (Q 70:43); God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137) — this after you have prayed four rakʿas: the first with the Mother of the Qurʾān and Yā-Sīn; the second with the Mother of the Qurʾān and Sūrat al-Dukhān; the third with the Mother of the Qurʾān and Tanzīl al-Sajda; and the fourth with the Mother of the Qurʾān and Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion, and He is powerful over everything (Q 67:1). And you say in the last prostration: Glory be to Him who has clothed Himself in might and spoken by it. Glory be to Him who has enwrapped Himself in majesty and shown Himself noble by it. Glory be to Him who has numbered everything in His knowledge. Glory be to Him to whom alone glorification is due. Glory be to Him who, when He wills a thing, has but to say to it "Be", and it is. Glory be to Him: what He wills comes to be, and what He does not will does not come to be. Glory be to the Possessor of favour, grace, and blessings. Glory be to the Possessor of knowledge and forbearance. Glory be to the Possessor of abundant bounty and grace. Glory be to the Possessor of the Throne, the Tablet, the Pen, and the Light. Then you raise your head and say: O God, I ask You by the bonds of might from Your Throne, and by the utmost reach of mercy from Your Book; I ask You by Your name, the Magnificent, the

Greatest, and by Your countenance, the Generous, the Most Generous, and by Your perfect words, that You make subservient to me a helper from among the righteous believing jinn, that he may aid me in what I desire of the needs of this world and the next. For seven persons of their nobles and their great ones will appear to you, and they will take visible form before you. And they will be [present]: before you recite the names, you will already have hung upon yourself seven warrants upon a thread, like a ṭarṭūr (a tall conical cap), and hung them upon your head; and that is to be before you begin the prayer. And you are to have wax with you. Then, when they are present before you, you take the first warrant of the seven warrants which you wrote and recited in the prayer, and you recite it over them and say: Which of you is the owner of this warrant and the owner of this note? And one of them will say: I am its owner. Then you say: What is your name? And he will say to you: My name is So-and-so son of So-and-so. So you write his name at the top of the note. Then you say to him: Hand over your seal. And you take /fol. 37v./ the thread and the wax and seal the bottom of the note as one seals a deed (ṣakk) — that is, the written document. Then you return his seal to him. And you say the like of that to each one of them, until you come to the seventh. Then you say: I conjure you by the names that are in these notes, that you present yourselves and answer my call whenever I call you, in obedience. Then you say: Depart; may God bless you, and [His blessing be] upon you. Then you lay away the deeds — that is, those warrants and those sealed documents — in a pure place, until some need appears to you: of food, or drink, or knowledge of some thing, or some buried treasure, or some hidden thing, or other than that. Then you call upon them, and they answer you swifter than lightning and wind, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And beware, my brother, of performing that while you are not strong of heart and firm of resolve. So if you are firm in your intellect, of lofty aspiration, steady of brain and strong of heart, and you are practised in the sciences, then set about this operation of yours if you have need of it. But if you are not firm of heart, and are heavy of head, then beware of their presence, for you will harm your spirit — for they are mighty destroyers. And guard yourself against beholding them, for [thereby] the veil of the heart is stripped away. And if you confine yourself to the eightfold signet (al-muthamman) mentioned above, that is a healing sufficiency, if God, exalted is He, wills.

And whoever writes the signet upon gazelle parchment and hangs it upon one who suffers bodily pains — such as fevers, chills, and the like — and [uses it] for the operations of concord (iʾtilāf) and for looking into the outcomes of affairs: God, blessed and exalted, does not fail to show him wonders in that. And that is because the secrets of the numbers possess an intellective power; for the numbers point to the letters by way of reception, and the letters point to the numbers by way of ascent; and the numbers point to the spiritual world, while the letters point to the corporeal world — and within it there is a spiritual [world]; and the letters become manifest through the subtleties of the corporeal things, while the numbers become manifest through the subtleties of the spiritual things. So whoever understands the secret of the mīm, to him is disclosed the secret of the ringing of the bell, by which comes the revelation of the sending-down (al-waḥy al-tanzīlī). And the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — was asked: How does the revelation come to you, O Messenger of God? And he — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((It comes to me at times like the ringing of a bell; and at times the angel takes visible form for me in the likeness of a man, and speaks to me, and I retain what he says.)) And the bell (jaras) is the jaljal. Do you not see, when they are gathered together upon the necks of the horses, upon their manes and their [trappings?], and the horses stir in their going, how there arises for the bell a resounding that is heard at a far distance? Such, then, is the manner of the revelation in the ringing of the bell. And the Prophet — blessings and peace be upon him — said: ((And that is the hardest of it upon me; then it leaves off from me, and I have retained what he said.)) And the likening of the letter mīm to the bell came about only because of its roundness, its closure, the gravity of its affair, and its dreadfulness. Do you not hear his saying — blessings and peace be upon him — concerning the description of Isrāfīl — peace be upon him — /fol. 38r./ and the immensity of his frame, his strength, and his obedience; and how upon his shoulder rests one of the legs of the Throne, for all its immensity; and then the Preserved Tablet is between his eyes, for all its immensity and the greatness of its bulk; and then the Trumpet, which is in breadth a journey of five hundred years — and it is said that it has many branches likewise. And he has set the Trumpet in his mouth, and has put one foot forward and set a foot back; the other of his two feet would surely pierce the seven earths to their utmost bounds. So consider his saying: ((He has taken the Trumpet into his mouth)) — how the mīm stood in the last position in [the word] iltaqama; for by the Trumpet come the terror, the swooning, and the raising [of the dead]. And he stands with his gaze fixed upon the Throne, awaiting when he shall be commanded to blow the Trumpet. And the blowing issues forth only by the closing of the two lips, and the mīm issues forth by the closing of the two lips; and one who pronounces it cannot bring it forth otherwise than by the closing of the two lips. For that reason it stood in the likening to the ringing of the bell; and the ṣalṣala is the force of the sound. And know here the difference between the ringing of the bell and the dragging of the chain over the smooth rock — the [revelation] of the sending-down, the Israelite, the Mosaic: for the sensation of the ringing is a spiritual motion, whereas the dragging of the chain is a corporeal motion. And the mīm has two aspects: a celestial aspect, which is the first mīm, and a terrestrial aspect, which is the second mīm, in the relation of detailed exposition — thus:. And since the mīm has a secret in the celestial spiritual things and in the terrestrial corporeal things, the numbers too have a relation within the celestial things, and their letters have secrets within the terrestrial things. And it is a hot letter in general, and within it there is a moisture between two heats, in detail — and that is the letter yāʾ; and the two heats are the two mīms, the first and the last, thus:. And from these two heats came its closing and its agitation. And were it not for the moist yāʾ that separates the two heats, the two Akhshab mountains would close together. So know [this]. And by the letter mīm was completed the concealed Name, the exalted, the most exalted — and it is bism. And now we shall expound the three noble and mighty names, which are Allāh, al-Raḥmān, al-Raḥīm. As for His name Allāh, exalted is He, it is the Greatest Name, comprehending all the [other] names; and for that reason He began His Book with it and sealed His Book with it, and by it He made His servants worship, and to it He pointed, and by it He made Himself known. And that is by reason of His saying, exalted is He: He is God (Q 59:22) — glorified be He. So He is the one pointed to in His names.

And whoever writes the letter mīm, and its figure and its wafq, and recites over it the words and the verses that follow, and carries it, and goes in with it upon kings and governors and the judges of Islam, is accepted in their sight and his word prevails; and awe accrues to its bearer, so that were he to confront lions with it, they would abase themselves before him and stand in awe of him. And if its bearer enters into war, he subdues the enemies and crushes the adversaries, and no enemy draws near him but God, exalted is He, gives him victory over him. And he will be beloved among the people, held in esteem and honoured; everyone who sees him loves him and inclines toward him. And it has mighty occult properties. /fol. 38v./

And some of the imams have indicated that whoever makes his striving (mujāhada) and his discipline (riyāḍa) sincere, and frees himself from the hand of appetite and of anger and of base characteristics and evil deeds; and sits in an empty place, and closes off the road of the senses, and opens the eye of the inward and its hearing; and sets the heart in correspondence with the world of the Dominion (ʿālam al-malakūt); and strives, and says "Allāh, Allāh" continually with the heart and not with the tongue, until he comes to have no existence of himself, and remains not seeing

— anything but God, exalted is He, there is opened for him an aperture through which he looks, and he beholds in waking what he beholds in sleep. So there appear to him the spirits of the angels and of the prophets, and beautiful, comely forms; and the Dominion (malakūt) of the heavens and the earth is unveiled to him, and he sees what it is not possible to expound nor to describe — as the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((The earth was drawn together for me, and I saw its easts and its wests.)) And God, exalted is He, said to His Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — in His Mighty Book: And remember the name of your Lord, and devote yourself to Him with utter devotion (Q 73:8). Its meaning is: the severing [of attachment] from everything, and the purifying of the heart of everything, and the imploring of Him with one's whole being. And this is the way of the Sufis in this age.

And know that among the occult properties of Lordship is the knowledge of His Most Beautiful Names and of His supreme, exalted attributes — and especially, among them, the Greatest Name of God. For He is God, who alone is singled out by this name, by His majesty and His glory; and He is the God to whom divinity belongs from Himself, by Himself; and He is God, who has no child and no parent: God is only one God (Q 4:171). And for that reason one of the friends of God (awliyāʾ) said to one of the aspirants: Do you wish to learn a benefit of which you are capable? He said: Yes. So he said to him: Persevere in saying "Allāh, Allāh, Allāh" for seven days, mentioning none but Him; and fast your day, and rise [in prayer] in your night as much as you are able; and persevere in this litany of remembrance, not parting from it by night nor by day, and speak to no one; and withdraw into retreat away from people for seven days — and the wonders of the earth will be shown to you. Then continue in that for another seven days — and the wonders of the heavens will be shown to you. Then likewise for another seven days — and the wonders of the highest Dominion will be shown to you. And if you attain to forty days, God, exalted is He, will manifest to you charismatic marvels (karāmāt), and will grant you free disposal (taṣarruf) in existence.

And it is related from the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — that he said: ((When the believing servant says: Yā Allāh (O God) — God, exalted is He, says: At your service, My servant! I am God; what is your need?)) God knows God best; none knows the innermost reality (kunh) of God's greatness but God. He is the Lord of all, and He is Knower of all things. And people have spoken concerning the innermost reality of God, exalted is He — whether it is knowable to human beings or not. He who accepts that it is not knowable to human beings says: because a thing is known by direct sight when it is present, and by likeness when it is absent; whereas God, exalted is He — the like of whom there is nothing (Q 42:11) — and He is not attained by direct sight, because of His saying, exalted is He: Sight does not attain Him, but He attains all sight (Q 6:103). And one of the masters among the verifiers (muḥaqqiqūn) said: since His pre-eternity, exalted is He, is established without beginning /fol. 39r./ and His perduring without cessation, and His unicity is not [a unicity] of number, and His attributes fall outside the attributes of creation, it necessarily follows that those who describe cannot reach the innermost reality of His attribute; for were it so, there would appear for it a limit and a likeness, and limit and likeness lead to passing away and annihilation, and that, in respect of God, exalted is He, is impossible. So said al-Muḥāsibī — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him. And it is related that Gabriel — peace be upon him — came down upon the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — with the Greatest Name upon a leaf from the leaves of the Garden, sealed with a seal of musk, on which was written: O God, I ask You by Your Name, the treasured, the concealed, the pure, the purified, the All-Holy, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate, the Possessor of Majesty and Honour. Anas said: A woman said: Teach it to us, O Messenger of God! And the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((We have been forbidden to teach it to women and children.)) And one of the excellent ones wrote to one of the righteous imams, [asking] that he gather for him formulae with which he might supplicate in the weighty matters of his affairs. So he wrote out for him this supplication, saying: O God, I ask You by Your Name; and by [the truth] that You are God in the realities of pure realization; and by [the truth] that You are God in every state among the states of majesty and equitable ordering; and by [the truth] that You are God, sanctified by the properties proper to oneness (aḥadiyya) and to self-sufficiency (ṣamadiyya), above [having] an opposite, a peer, a contrary, or an equal; and by [the truth] that You are God, the like of whom there is nothing, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing (Q 42:11) — that You bless our master Muḥammad, and the family of Muḥammad, and everyone who loves Muḥammad; and that You bless him; and that You fulfil all my needs, every one of them, with a fulfilment wherein there is for me the good of this world and of the hereafter — preserved by [Your] watchful keeping, preserved from calamities, regarded with the special properties of [Your] providential care. O You who return again and again with good things! O You who are in reality worthy of pious reverence and worthy of [bestowing] good things! O God, this is the request of a servant of the might of Your Lordship, in the making manifest of his request, by [the truth] that You are the Knower of the unseen realms, and the Witness of the realities of the things sought before ever they come into contact with hearts. So bring it to completion with a beautiful ending, O best of all that is sought. And may God bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad, the beloved of hearts. And it is said that this supplication contains the Greatest Name of God, just as has been transmitted concerning "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". And know that between it [the basmala] and the Greatest Name of God there is only what lies between the black of the eye and the white of it.
